title: LLMs Cannot Be Neutral: Gender Sensitivity Across Candidates, Evaluators, and Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.02692v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate candidates for professional roles, raising concerns about their sensitivity to demographic identities. We examine how candidate and evaluator gender assignments affect decisions by LLM-as-a-Judge (LaJ) models and decision language models (DLMs). In a hypothetical city council voting task, eight models evaluated 240 synthetic professional narratives from NVIDIA's US and French Nemotron-Personas datasets under independently varied gender assignments, producing 30,720 judgments. Explicit candidate gender labels increased Yes-vote probability by 1.05-1.73 percentage points relative to unspecified gender, while only the nonbinary evaluator assignment showed a significant increase (1.26 points). Identity matching showed no significant overall association. Yes-vote rates varied across models (81.3-97.2%), and 2.5-3.3% of decisions reversed relative to the unspecified-identity baseli

translated_title: 大语言模型无法保持中立：候选人、评估者与模型中的性别敏感性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于评估专业职位的候选人，这引发了人们对其对人口统计身份敏感性的担忧。我们研究了候选人性别设定和评估者性别设定如何影响“大模型作为评判者”（LLM-as-a-Judge, LaJ）模型和决策语言模型（DLMs）的决策。在一个假设的市议会投票任务中，八个模型在独立变化的性别设定下，对来自NVIDIA美国和法国Nemotron-Personas数据集的240个合成职业叙事进行了评估，共产生了30,720个判断。相对于未指定性别的情况，明确的候选人性别标签使投赞成票的概率增加了1.05-1.73个百分点，而只有非二元性别评估者的设定显示出显著增加（1.26个百分点）。身份匹配未显示出显著的总体关联。各模型的赞成票比率存在差异（81.3%-97.2%），并且相对于未指定身份的基线，2.5%-3.3%的决策发生了逆转。
tldr: 该研究通过对八个模型在市议会投票任务中的30,720次判断分析，发现大语言模型在评估候选人时无法保持性别中立，明确的性别标签会显著影响其投票决策，且不同模型之间的决策行为存在显著差异。
en_tdlr: Large language models cannot remain neutral when evaluating candidates—explicit gender labels significantly shift their voting decisions, and decision behavior varies substantially across models.
